the preparation and characterization of Pd Nb doped organosilosica membranes for H 2 /CO 2 separation.
the preparation of Pd Nb BTE SE membranes for H2 CO2 separation.
the preparation of Pd Nb BTESe membranes by different metal priority doping routes for H 2/CO 2 separation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bimetallic doping is a promising way to improve the performance of organosilicas membranes for H2 separation.

bimetallic doping of organosilicas is an effective method for simultaneously improving H permeance and permselectivity of organosilicon membranes for H/CO2 separation by the synergistic effects of the two metal dopants, and Pd Nb bimetallized BTESE membranes with Pd doping prior are promising candidates for H/CO separation.
the metal doping route can be a key factor in determining the gas separation performance of Pd Nb doped organoslicia membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pd and Nb co-doping is more efficient than monometallic doping in terms of H2 permeance, H2/CO permselectivity and H2/He permselectivity.

Pd Nb bimetals can be doped into the BTESE framework by the different doping routes, and the PNB Pd membranes with the highest surface area, pore volume and Pd loading exhibit the best H2 permeance as well as H2/CO 2 permselectivity.

the PNB Pd membranes with Pd doping prior to the Nb doping exhibit a higher H2 permeance, a higher H2/CO 2 permselectivity and a higher H2/N2 permselectivity, comparing with PNB PdNb membranes with Nb doping prior to the Pd doping.
